Order 
This criminal revision under Section 102 of Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act,
2015 has been filed by the applicant against the order dated 29/11/2024 passed in Cr.A.No.86/2024 by Juvenile Court and II Additional Sessions Judge and Special Judge (POCSO Act), Jhabua (M.P.),
whereby the order passed by the Juvenile Justice Board, Jhabua in Criminal Case No.300/2023 on 08/11/2024 in respect of Crime No.830/2023 registered at Police Station Ranapur, District Jhabua under Sections 376, 376(A)(B), 376(2)(Ch) and 377 of Indian Penal Code, 1860 and Section 5(n)/9 and 5(m)/6 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, denying the benefit of bail to the applicant / juvenile in conflict with law has been up held.
2.

3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is innocent NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:9515 2 CRR-6403-2024 and has falsely been implicated in the crime.
There is no sufficient evidence available on record to establish the complicity of the accused with the alleged crime.
He is suffering jail incarceration since 07/12/2023.
Learned Courts below have not taken into account the mandatory provisions as contained under Section 12 of the JJ Act, 2015.
Probation Officer report is also in favour of the applicant.
Six witnesses including victim and her parents have been examined before the trial Court.
There is no likelihood of his absconsion leaving his family or tampering with evidence.
Final conclusion of the trial will take considerable long time.
Applicant may come in contact with criminals, which may spoil his future.

sentences.text: that parents of the juvenile will take care of him and he will abide by all the terms and conditions as imposed by this Court, therefore, pray for allowing the revision by setting aside the orders passed by both the Courts below and the juvenile be given on Supurdagi to his parents.

4. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent / State has vehemently opposed the prayer and prays for dismissal of the bail application on the ground that heinous offence has been committed by the applicant on the toddler of 05 years of age.

However, he fairly admits that a report from the Probation Officer regarding social status of the juvenile / applicant has been received and nothing adverse has been mentioned therein against the applicant.
He further submits that applicant has no criminal antecedent.

5. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
6.
The mandate of Section 12 of Act of 2015 is the only mandate, which is to be seen at the time of giving minor in the custody of his parents or guardian if no such danger is apparent.

7. In the aforesaid factual backdrop, looking to the mandate of Section 12 of the Act of 2015, report of Probation Officer coupled with period of custody, NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:9515 3 CRR-6403-2024 this Court is inclined to grant benefit of bail to the applicant / juvenile.
Accordingly, without commenting on the merits of the case, the criminal revision is allowed.
8. Looking to the mandate of Section 12 of the Act of 2015, revision is allowed and orders passed by both the Courts below are hereby set aside.

It is directed that the custody of the applicant / juvenile be given to his parents / guardian till the final conclusion of the pending case before the Juvenile Justice Board, Jhabua on furnishing a personal bond of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only)
with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Juvenile Justice Board with undertaking therein that parents / guardian will take care of juvenile and will take care that he will not indulge in any kind of criminal activities in future.
9. With the aforesaid, criminal revision stands allowed and disposed off.
Certified copy as per rules.

(BINOD KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE Tej Child In Conflict With Law Minor Arjun ... vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/60797176/
